slides.0.title: Viticulture in Depth
slides.0.subtitle: Training, water and risk management
slides.1.title: Santorini: viticulture at the extreme
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Kouloura and koulouraki
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Kouloura is basket training with fruit grown inside the basket; koulouraki is a lower gobelet. Both protect against the strong northerly winds
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Soil
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Volcanic: basalt, ash, sand, pumice and andesite; sandy with very little clay; self-rooted and never hit by phylloxera
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Morning mist
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Morning mist from the caldera supplies moisture in drought; rain is scarce and farming is largely dry
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Very low yields
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The PDO cap is 6.5 t/ha and practice is usually under 3 t/ha
slides.1.content: Essay spine: wind → low training; drought and poor sandy soil → low yields and concentration; no phylloxera → old, self-rooted vines.
slides.2.title: High and cool sites
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Naoussa: 150–400 m
slides.2.highlights.0.content: South- and south-east-facing slopes; at least 25 soil types in limestone, clay, loam, schist and sand families
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Mantineia: 650–800 m
slides.2.highlights.1.content: One of Greece's coldest zones, where Moschofilero is often harvested in October
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Nemea: 200–850 m
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Big day–night swings; higher sites keep aroma and acidity
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Amyndeo and Zitsa
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Cool climates yielding lighter styles such as sparkling and rosé
slides.2.content: Link for essays: altitude → diurnal range → retained acidity and aroma → sparkling, rosé and fresh whites.
slides.3.title: Water and climate stress: the Santorini case
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Heat and drought, 2023–2025
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A university professor said 2023 and 2024 were the hottest in 60 years; a 90-year-old kouloura vine died of heat and drought
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Collapse in output
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Santorini's Assyrtiko output fell from about 2,500 tonnes in 2022 to about 500 tonnes last year, 2025 (Reuters, June 2026)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Grape prices
slides.3.highlights.2.content: About €10 per kg on Santorini versus about €0.80 in northern Greece
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Adaptation
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Trials of treated-wastewater irrigation, row planting, subsurface irrigation with trellising, and atmospheric water harvesting
slides.3.content: A ready case for Diploma climate and sustainability questions: problem (heat, drought) → consequence (yield, price, quality) → response (irrigation, planting) → tension between tradition and adaptation.
slides.4.title: Old vines, yields and diversity
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Old bush vines
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Many old vines are bush-trained and dry-farmed: low-yielding and drought-tolerant; one Naoussa single vineyard has vines over 85 years old
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Legal versus actual yield
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Naoussa's legal cap is 70 hl/ha, while quality-minded producers often aim for 35 hl/ha or less
slides.4.highlights.2.title: 300+ native varieties
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Diversity is both an asset and a challenge for recognition and market communication
slides.4.content: For risk management, list wind, drought, frost/heat and disease, each with one Greek example.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What is the main function of Santorini's kouloura?
A. Keeping fruit inside the basket, shielding it from wind and sun
Kouloura is a training response to strong wind and drought.
Which is a major recent stress on Santorini?
A. Severe heat and drought sharply cutting output
Assyrtiko output fell from about 2,500 t in 2022 to about 500 t in 2025.
What altitude and aspect characterise Naoussa's vineyards?
A. 150–400 m, south and south-east facing
